dossier.role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO of Eldridge Industries, and Chairman of Eldridge
dossier.thesis: Eldridge is a holding company that uses long-term capital from its own insurance businesses (Security Benefit and Everly Life) to build and back companies across insurance, asset management, technology, real estate, sports and media. In sports and media it focuses on companies that own premium intellectual property.

brief.headline: Eldridge backs businesses built around premium IP, and your app monetizes the fanbases around live-event IP, with Qloo showing strong customer overlap with A24, Fanatics and Overtime (fit score 82).
brief.angle: Pitch yourself as a technology layer that extends premium sports and entertainment IP into the full night out (bars, merch, rides), rather than as a standalone consumer app. Be upfront that you are earlier than Eldridge's usual established or growth-stage targets, and show how a strategic minority stake could scale across its sports and media holdings.

name_drop.line: Your customers show the highest affinity with A24 (0.767) in our data, which suggests they follow culture-defining brands with devoted fanbases, the same kind of fans we turn into a full night out.
name_drop.name: A24

name_drop.line: Fanatics has a 0.76 affinity with our customers, so the fans buying merch on our app already behave like the fans in that ecosystem.
name_drop.name: Fanatics

name_drop.line: We saw Eldridge led a strategic round in Overtime, and our customers show a 0.727 affinity with it; we reach a slightly older 25–29 crowd, which could extend that audience as it grows up.
name_drop.name: Overtime

deck: Lead with the premium IP angle: show how each fanbase (artist, team, venue) gets its own curated pre-show, merch and ride experience.
Show the 25–29 audience next to Eldridge's under-25 portfolio crowd, framed as the next life stage of the fans its media and sports assets already attract.
Use Ticketmaster, Spotify and Uber as comparables for ticketing, fan-level personalization and ride logistics, but show clearly how you combine them into one night-out product.
Include a slide on how your personalization technology could scale across Eldridge's sports and media holdings, since it looks for businesses that can spread technology across its portfolio.
Be explicit about stage and structure: say what you are asking for and how a strategic minority stake and long-term partnership would work.

openers.line: Game nights at Lakers games are a night out in themselves, with the pre-game bars, merch and getting home. That full-evening experience is what we build for concert fans.
openers.name: Los Angeles Lakers

openers.line: A24 has built a fanbase that identifies with the brand itself. We do something similar at the fanbase level, shaping each night out around the crowd attending.
openers.name: A24

openers.line: Our team has been reading about the Showtime-era Lakers, and what stands out is how much of the dynasty was an experience around the game. That's the idea behind our product.
openers.based_on: Showtime: Magic, Kareem, Riley, and the Los Angeles Lakers Dynasty of the 1980s
openers.name: Showtime: Magic, Kareem, Riley, and the Los Angeles Lakers Dynasty of the 1980s

avoid: Don't pitch as a typical seed or early-stage venture bet; Eldridge mostly backs established or growth-stage assets, so be clear on your stage and why it fits.
Don't lean on generic consumer-app metrics without tying them to premium IP, which is the sports and media focus.
Don't present it as a quick-flip story; Eldridge invests with long-term, permanent capital and will want a durable, scalable business.
questions: Why would Eldridge, which mostly backs established or growth-stage companies, invest at your stage?
How do you win and keep the relationships with artists, teams, venues and ticketing platforms whose IP your experiences depend on?
How could your technology scale across other sports and media assets, and what would that look like in practice?
